references.text: The daily burnt offering (tamid) that was to be offered morning and evening, which forms the basis for the additional festival offerings mentioned in Numbers 28:24.
The requirement to offer a fire offering to the Lord for seven days during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
The description of the daily burnt offering (olat hatamid) that is cited as the foundation for the festival offerings.
The context of verse 24, which describes the specific sacrifices to be brought during the Passover festival.
A parallel formulation stating that festival offerings are to be added to the daily burnt offering and its drink offering.
The burnt offering as a pleasing aroma (reach nichoach) to the Lord - the same expression is used.
The term 'lechem isheh' (fire offering bread/fire offering food) for the Lord.
Ezekiel's vision of the daily burnt offering in the future temple, which continues the principle of the tamid offering.
